questions.q: The line $L_1$ joining the two points $(-1,2)$ and $(3,6)$ divides the line $L_2$ which passes through $(3,-1)$ in the ratio 1:3 internally, then the equation of $L_2$ is
questions.explanation: The point dividing $(-1,2)$ and $(3,6)$ in ratio 1:3 is $\left(\dfrac{3-3}{4},\dfrac{6+6}{4}\right)=(0,3)$. $L_2$ through $(3,-1)$ and $(0,3)$ has slope $-\dfrac43$, giving $4x+3y-9=0$.

questions.q: A line passes through (-1, -3) and perpendicular to x + 6y = 5. Its x intercept is
questions.explanation: Given line has slope -1/6, so perpendicular slope is 6; line: y+3=6(x+1); setting y=0 gives x = -1/2.

questions.q: The angle between the line $x+y=3$ and the line joining the points $(1,1)$ and $(-3,4)$ is
questions.explanation: Slope of $x+y=3$ is $m_1=-1$; slope of the joining line is $m_2=-\dfrac{3}{4}$. $\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1m_2}\right|=\dfrac{1}{7}$.

questions.q: A line passes through $(2, 2)$ and is perpendicular to the line $3x + y = 3$. Its y-intercept is
questions.explanation: Slope of $3x+y=3$ is $-3$, so perpendicular slope is $1/3$. Line: $y-2=\dfrac{1}{3}(x-2)$, giving y-intercept $= 2-\dfrac{2}{3}=\dfrac{4}{3}$.

questions.q: If the straight line 2x - 3y + 17 = 0 is perpendicular to the line passing through the points (7, 17) and (15, β), then β equals
questions.explanation: The given line has slope $2/3$, so the perpendicular slope is $-3/2$. $\frac{\beta-17}{15-7}=-\frac32\Rightarrow\beta=17-12=5$.

questions.q: The equation of straight line which passes through the point (a cos$^3\theta$, a sin$^3\theta$) and perpendicular to x sec$\theta$ + y cosec$\theta$ = a is
options: x cos$\theta$ $-$ y sin$\theta$ = a cos2$\theta$
x cos$\theta$ + y sin$\theta$ = a cos2$\theta$
questions.explanation: The given line has slope $-\tan\theta$, so the perpendicular has slope $\cot\theta$; using the point, the line simplifies to x cos$\theta$ $-$ y sin$\theta$ = a cos2$\theta$.

questions.q: The two lines $lx + my = n$ and $l'x + m'y = n'$ are perpendicular if
questions.explanation: Slopes are $-l/m$ and $-l'/m'$; perpendicularity gives $(-l/m)(-l'/m')=-1 \Rightarrow ll'+mm'=0$.

questions.q: A line cuts off equal intercepts on the co-ordinate axes. The angle made by this line with the positive direction of X-axis is
questions.explanation: Equal intercepts give the line $x+y=a$, with slope $-1$, so the angle with the positive X-axis is $135^\circ$.

questions.q: The equation of the line parallel to the line $3x-4y+2=0$ and passing through $(-2,3)$ is
questions.explanation: Line $3x-4y+c=0$ through $(-2,3)$: $-6-12+c=0\Rightarrow c=18$.

questions.q: Equation of line passing through the point $(1,2)$ and perpendicular to the line $y=3x-1$ is
questions.explanation: Slope of the given line is 3, so the perpendicular slope is $-\dfrac13$; the line through $(1,2)$ is $y-2=-\dfrac13(x-1) \Rightarrow x+3y-7=0$.

questions.q: If the straight lines $2x + 3y - 3 = 0$ and $x + ky + 7 = 0$ are perpendicular, then the value of k is
questions.explanation: Slopes are $-2/3$ and $-1/k$; perpendicularity gives $\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{k}\right)=-1 \Rightarrow k=-2/3$.

questions.q: A line passes through $(2, 2)$ and is perpendicular to the line $3x+y=3$; its y-intercept is ____
questions.explanation: Perpendicular slope $=1/3$; line: $y-2=\dfrac13(x-2)$. At $x=0$, $y=\dfrac43$.

questions.q: A straight line passes through the points (5, 0) and (0, 3). The length of perpendicular from the point (4, 4) on the line is
questions.explanation: The line is $3x+5y-15=0$. Distance from (4,4): $\dfrac{|12+20-15|}{\sqrt{34}}=\dfrac{17}{\sqrt{34}}=\sqrt{17/2}$.

questions.q: If the line $6x-7y+8+\lambda(3x-y+5)=0$ is parallel to y-axis, then $\lambda=$
questions.explanation: The coefficient of y must vanish: $-7-\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-7$.

questions.q: The angle between the lines $\sin^2\alpha\cdot y^2-2xy\cos^2\alpha+(\cos^2\alpha-1)x^2=0$ is
questions.explanation: Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}$ with $a+b=0$ here, the angle is $90°$.

questions.q: The minimum area of the triangle formed by the variable line $3\cos\theta\cdot x+4\sin\theta\cdot y=12$ and the co-ordinate axes is
questions.explanation: Area $=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{4}{\cos\theta}\cdot\dfrac{3}{\sin\theta}=\dfrac{12}{\sin2\theta}$, minimized at $\sin2\theta=1$ giving area 12.

questions.q: The points $(11, 9)$, $(2, 1)$ and $(2, -1)$ are the midpoints of the sides of the triangle. Then the centroid is
questions.explanation: The centroid of a triangle equals the centroid of the triangle formed by its midpoints: $\left(\dfrac{11+2+2}{3},\dfrac{9+1-1}{3}\right)=(5,3)$.

questions.q: The reflection of the point $(1, 1)$ along the line $y = -x$ is
questions.explanation: Reflection of $(a,b)$ in the line $y=-x$ is $(-b,-a)$, so $(1,1)$ maps to $(-1,-1)$.

questions.q: The number of circles that touch the co-ordinate axes and the line whose slope is $-1$ and $y$-intercept is $1$, is
questions.explanation: Circles tangent to both axes have centres $(\pm r,\pm r)$. Imposing tangency to the line $x+y=1$ gives 2 valid circles with centre $(r,r)$ and 1 each with centres $(r,-r)$ and $(-r,r)$, totalling 4.

questions.q: If one of the slopes of the pair of lines $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$ is $n$ times the other then
questions.explanation: With $m_1=nm_2$, $m_1+m_2=-2h/b$ and $m_1m_2=a/b$. Eliminating $m_2$ gives $4nh^2=(n+1)^2ab$.

questions.q: Locus of a point which moves such that its distance from the $X$-axis is twice its distance from the line $x-y=0$ is ............
questions.explanation: $|y|=2\cdot\dfrac{|x-y|}{\sqrt2}$. Squaring, $y^2=2(x-y)^2$, which simplifies to $2x^2-4xy+y^2=0$.
Slope of $AB=\dfrac{4-2}{2-1}=2$ and slope of $BC=\dfrac{8-4}{4-2}=2$; equal slopes through a common point mean the three points are collinear, forming a straight line.

questions.q: If lines represented by $x+3y-6=0$, $2x+y-4=0$ and $kx-3y+1=0$ are concurrent, then the value of $k$ is ............
questions.explanation: Solving the first two lines gives the intersection $\left(\dfrac{6}{5},\dfrac{8}{5}\right)$. Substituting into $kx-3y+1=0$ gives $6k-19=0$, so $k=\dfrac{19}{6}$.

questions.q: The line joining $A(2, -7)$ and $B(6, 5)$ is divided into 4 equal parts by the points $P, Q$ and $R$ such that $AQ=RP=QB$. The midpoint of $PR$ is
questions.explanation: $P,Q,R$ divide $AB$ into four equal parts, so $Q$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and, by symmetry, also the midpoint of $PR$: $Q=\left(\dfrac{2+6}{2},\dfrac{-7+5}{2}\right)=(4,-1)$.

questions.q: Let $P\equiv(-1, 0)$, $Q\equiv(0, 0)$ and $R\equiv(3, 3\sqrt3)$ be three points. The equation of the bisector of the angle $PQR$ is
questions.explanation: Unit vectors along $QP$ and $QR$ are $(-1,0)$ and $(1/2,\sqrt3/2)$; their sum $(-1/2,\sqrt3/2)$ gives the bisector direction, with slope $-\sqrt3$, i.e. $\sqrt3x+y=0$.

questions.q: The foot of the perpendicular from the point $(2, 4)$ upon $x + y = 4$ is
The vertices of a triangle are $(6, 0)$, $(0, 6)$ and $(6, 6)$. The distance between its circumcentre and centroid is
questions.explanation: This is a right triangle (right angle at $(6,6)$), so the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse $=(3,3)$; the centroid is $(4,4)$; the distance between them is $\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt2$.
